x-remigio-legat

Remigio Legat was an Italian painter of the 1800s who painted scenes from the Risorgimento, the movement that united Italy. His picture of the Battle of Calatafimi was painted in 1860, soon after Garibaldi's victory.

Robert Gibb was a Scottish painter born in Edinburgh in 1845. He painted battles and military scenes, became the Painter and Limner to the Queen in Scotland and was Keeper of the National Gallery of Scotland. He died in Edinburgh in 1932.

Hippolyte Bellangé was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted soldiers and battle scenes, many from Napoleon's armies, and later served as curator of the museum in Rouen. He died in Paris in 1866.

Eugène Lami was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He painted elegant scenes of the court and big battle pictures for King Louis-Philippe, and moved easily between fashion and war. He died in Paris in 1890.
Thomas Jones Barker was an English painter born in Bath in 1815. He painted Crimean War scenes and popular pictures of the British army, and lived in London, where he died in 1882.

William Simpson was a Scottish war artist, born in Glasgow in 1823. He worked as a correspondent for the Illustrated London News and was sent to the Crimean War, drawing what he saw for newspapers at home, and later traveled to India, Abyssinia and elsewhere. He died in London in 1899.
x-elizabeth-thompson-lady-butler

Elizabeth Thompson, later Lady Butler, was a British painter born in Lausanne, Switzerland, in 1846. She became one of the most popular battle painters of Victorian Britain, starting with her Roll Call in 1874. She married a general, lived in Ireland, and died in 1933.
x-grigory-shukaev
Grigory Shukaev was a Russian painter of the 1800s who made a picture of the Siege of Sevastopol in 1856, soon after the end of the Crimean War. Not much is known about his life.

Benjamin Robert Haydon was an English painter born in Plymouth in 1786. He wanted to be a great painter of history, made huge pictures and also lively group portraits, but was always in debt. He lived in London and died there in 1846.

Eastman Johnson was an American painter born in Lovell, Maine, in 1824. He studied in Düsseldorf and The Hague, lived in New York and painted warm scenes of American life, including pictures related to the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1906.

Francis Bicknell Carpenter was an American painter born in Homer, New York, in 1830. He lived for six months at the White House in 1864 to paint Abraham Lincoln and his cabinet, and he died in New York City in 1900.

François-Auguste Biard was a French painter born in Lyon in 1799. He traveled widely to Lapland and Brazil, painted exotic scenes and political pictures, including one about the abolition of slavery in 1848. He died in Fontainebleau in 1882.

Carl Frederik von Breda was a Swedish painter born in Stockholm in 1759. He spent nine years in England, where he painted portraits, including one of the antislavery campaigner Thomas Clarkson, and later became court painter in Sweden. He died in Stockholm in 1818.

Johann Moritz Rugendas was a German painter born in Augsburg in 1802. He traveled and lived in Brazil, Mexico and Chile, producing many sketches of landscapes, daily life and the lives of enslaved people. He died in Weilheim an der Teck in 1858.

Thomas Nast was an American cartoonist born in Landau, Germany, in 1840. He moved to New York as a child and became famous in Harper's Weekly for his political cartoons, and is credited with creating the Republican elephant and the modern Santa Claus. He died in Ecuador in 1902, where he served as US consul.
Alanson Fisher was an American portrait painter born in 1807. He lived mainly in New York, painting portraits of well-known people, including the author Harriet Beecher Stowe. He died in 1884.

Thure de Thulstrup was a Swedish-born American illustrator born in Stockholm in 1848. He served in the French army, moved to the United States and became famous for his illustrations of battles of the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1930.

Peter F. Rothermel was an American painter born in Nescopeck, Pennsylvania, in 1812. He worked in Philadelphia, where he painted huge canvases of historical subjects, including the Battle of Gettysburg for the state of Pennsylvania. He died in Linfield, Pennsylvania, in 1895.
x-kurz-and-allison

Kurz and Allison was an American printing firm in Chicago that made colorful lithographs of famous battles and historical scenes in the 1880s and 1890s. Their prints brought the Civil War into many homes.
x-currier-and-ives

Currier and Ives was a famous American printmaking firm based in New York, founded by Nathaniel Currier and James Ives, which published cheap hand-colored lithographs from 1857 to 1907. They sold millions of prints of news events, landscapes and everyday life.

Felix Octavius Carr Darley was an American illustrator born in Philadelphia in 1822. He illustrated books by Washington Irving and Charles Dickens and made many pictures of the Civil War. He died in Claymont, Delaware, in 1888.

Julian O. Davidson was an American marine painter born in Cumberland, Maryland, in 1853. He lived in New York, painting sea scenes and naval battles of the Civil War for popular prints. He died in 1894.

Mathew Brady was an American photographer born in New York State in 1822. He ran studios in New York and Washington, photographed presidents, and organized teams of photographers who recorded the Civil War. He died in New York City in 1896.

Timothy H. O'Sullivan was an American photographer born in Ireland or New York around 1840. He photographed the Civil War, including the dead at Gettysburg, and later made photographs of the American West. He died in New York in 1882.

Alfred Jacob Miller was an American painter born in Baltimore in 1810. In 1837 he traveled west to the Rocky Mountains and made the first paintings of the fur trade and Native American life there. He lived in Baltimore and died there in 1874.

Charles Marion Russell was an American painter born in St. Louis in 1864. He moved to Montana as a teenager, worked as a cowboy and lived among the Blackfeet, then became the most famous painter of the Old West. He lived in Great Falls, where he died in 1926.

Thomas Hill was an English-born American painter born in Birmingham in 1829. He grew up in Massachusetts and moved to California, where he painted huge landscapes of Yosemite and the Sierra Nevada. He died in Raymond, California, in 1908.
x-illustrator-b-h
This print was made by an illustrator who signed it with the initials B&H. Prints like this appeared in magazines and books to show readers far away what the West looked like.

Edgar Samuel Paxson was an American painter born in 1852. He moved to Montana as a young man, worked as a scout and mailman, and painted detailed pictures of the Western frontier, especially of the Battle of the Little Bighorn. He died in Missoula in 1919.

Ernest Meissonier was a French painter born in Lyon in 1815. He became famous for tiny, extremely detailed pictures, and later for big scenes of Napoleon's armies and the siege of Paris, where he served as an officer. He lived in Paris and Poissy and died in Paris in 1891.

Édouard Detaille was a French painter born in Paris in 1848. He studied with Meissonier and became the most celebrated painter of the French army, making huge, accurate pictures of the war of 1870 and of Napoleon's troops. He lived in Paris and died there in 1912.

Alphonse de Neuville was a French painter born in Saint-Omer in 1835. He became known for realistic scenes of the Franco-Prussian War, in which he had served, and for illustrating books. He lived in Paris and died there in 1885.

Édouard Castres was a Swiss painter born in Geneva in 1838. He volunteered as a Red Cross helper in the Franco-Prussian War and later painted the huge panorama of the Bourbaki army's retreat into Switzerland. He died in Annemasse, France, in 1902.

Charles Édouard Armand-Dumaresq was a French painter born in Paris in 1826. He painted military subjects and the French army, including scenes of the Franco-Prussian War. He lived and worked in Paris and died there in 1895.
Léon Sabatier was a French painter and lithographer born in Paris in 1800. He traveled widely, made views of cities and landscapes and recorded the burning of Paris in 1871. He died in Paris in 1887.

Jules Girardet was a French painter born in Paris in 1856, from a family of artists. He painted scenes of war and the French colonial empire, and illustrated books and magazines. He died in Boulogne-Billancourt in 1938.

Pierre Puvis de Chavannes was a French painter born in Lyon in 1824. He painted calm, pale murals for the Panthéon in Paris and other public buildings, in a style that influenced many later artists. He died in Paris in 1898.

Frédéric Théodore Lix was a French illustrator born in Strasbourg in 1830. He drew news pictures for magazines, such as L'Illustration, and recorded the war of 1870 and the Paris Commune. He lived in Paris and died there in 1897.
x-benjamin-moran

Benjamin Moran was the artist who designed the cover of the official program for the Woman Suffrage Procession in Washington on March 3, 1913, showing a woman on a white horse in front of the Capitol.

Henry Mayer, nicknamed Hy Mayer, was a cartoonist born in Worms, Germany, in 1868. He moved to the United States, where he became a popular cartoonist for Puck magazine and a pioneer of animated cartoons. He lived in New York and died in 1954.
Joseph Kyle was an American portrait painter born in Ohio in 1815. He worked in New York City, painting many portraits of his time, including the Quaker minister Lucretia Mott. He died in 1863.

Nina Evans Allender was an American cartoonist born in Auburn, New York, in 1873. She was the official cartoonist of the National Woman's Party and drew hundreds of cartoons for the fight for women's right to vote. She lived in Washington, D.C., and died in Plainfield, New Jersey, in 1957.
x-league-of-women-voters

The League of Women Voters was founded in 1920 by suffragist Carrie Chapman Catt, as women across the United States won the right to vote. The organization still teaches people about voting and publishes posters and guides.
x-national-woman-suffrage-publishing-co
The National Woman Suffrage Publishing Company printed posters, newspapers and flyers to win American women the vote. Its materials appeared around the country in the 1910s.

Rea Irvin was an American artist born in San Francisco in 1881. He drew magazine covers and cartoons, and designed the first cover of The New Yorker in 1925, featuring the dandy Eustace Tilley. He lived in New York and died in the Virgin Islands in 1972.

Merle De Vore Johnson was an American illustrator born in Oregon City in 1874. He drew posters and magazine covers and later became a well-known collector of rare books. He lived in New York and died there in 1935.

Paul Nash was an English painter born in London in 1889. He was an official war artist in both World Wars and painted haunting landscapes of broken trees and battlefields. He died in Boscombe, England, in 1946.

A. Y. Jackson was a Canadian painter born in Montreal in 1882. He was a founding member of the Group of Seven, an official war artist in World War I, and one of the painters who made rugged northern landscapes famous. He died in Kleinburg, Ontario, in 1974.

Alfred Bastien was a Belgian painter born in 1873. He painted huge panoramas, then during World War I he was a war artist for the Canadian War Memorials, making large paintings of the front at Passchendaele. He lived in Brussels and died in Uccle in 1955.
Frederick Thwaites Bush was an English artist born in Market Harborough in 1887. He made lithographs of scenes of the front, including Vimy Ridge, during World War I. He died in Greenwich in 1985.

C. R. W. Nevinson was an English painter born in London in 1889. He painted the war in the dynamic style of Futurism and was an official war artist in World War I. He lived in London and died in Hampstead in 1946.

Stanhope Forbes was an Irish-born English painter born in Dublin in 1857. He settled in Newlyn in Cornwall, where he painted fishermen and villagers in the open air, and founded an art school. He died in Newlyn in 1947.

Henry Ossawa Tanner was an African American painter born in Pittsburgh in 1859. He moved to Paris in 1891, became famous for his quiet religious paintings and was the first Black artist to win wide international fame. He died in Paris in 1937.

Wyndham Lewis was a painter and writer, born in 1882 on a yacht off the coast of Nova Scotia. He lived mostly in London, where he led Vorticism, a British avant-garde movement, and served as an artillery officer and official war artist in World War I. He died in London in 1957.

Will Longstaff was an Australian painter born in Ballarat in 1879. He served in World War I and then painted memorials to the missing, including Menin Gate at Midnight, which toured Australia and Britain. He died in Littlehampton, England, in 1953.

Boris Kustodiev was a Russian painter born in Astrakhan in 1878. He lived in Saint Petersburg and painted colorful scenes of Russian merchants and festivals, and after the revolution made pictures of it despite being paralyzed and working from a wheelchair. He died in 1927.

Ivan Vladimirov was a Russian painter born in Vilnius in 1869. He worked in Saint Petersburg and made large paintings and drawings of the revolutions of 1905 and 1917 as an eyewitness. He died in Leningrad in 1947.

Isaak Brodsky was a Russian painter born in 1884 in what is now Ukraine. He trained in Odessa, Saint Petersburg and Italy, and after the revolution became a leading Soviet painter, known for his portraits of Lenin. He died in Leningrad in 1939.

El Lissitzky was a Russian artist born in Pochinok in 1890. He worked as an architect, a painter and a designer, and made his famous poster of the Red Wedge in 1919. He lived in Vitebsk, Germany and Moscow, and died in Moscow in 1941.
x-stepan-mukharsky

Stepan Mukharsky was a Russian artist who made posters for the Soviet government during and after the Russian Civil War. His bright, cartoon-like posters were made to explain the revolution to people who could not read.

Wojciech Kossak was a Polish painter born in Paris in 1856 who lived in Kraków. He painted battle scenes, horses and moments from Poland's history, as part of a family of artists. He died in Kraków in 1942.
x-dorothea-lange

Dorothea Lange was an American photographer born in Hoboken, New Jersey, in 1895. She moved to San Francisco, and during the Great Depression worked for the government photographing the lives of poor farm families, creating the famous Migrant Mother. She died in San Francisco in 1965.
x-arthur-rothstein

Arthur Rothstein was an American photographer born in New York City in 1915. He was the first photographer hired by the government's Farm Security Administration, capturing the Dust Bowl, and later worked for Look magazine. He died in New Rochelle in 1985.

Walker Evans was an American photographer born in St. Louis in 1903. He photographed poor farm families for the government during the Depression, and his plain, honest style shaped documentary photography. He lived in New York and died in New Haven in 1975.

Russell Lee was an American photographer born in Ottawa, Illinois, in 1903. He worked for the Farm Security Administration, took thousands of pictures of rural life in the 1930s and 1940s, and later taught photography in Texas. He died in Austin in 1986.

Gordon Parks was an American photographer born in Fort Scott, Kansas, in 1912. He started as a government photographer, then worked for Life magazine, wrote books and directed the film Shaft. He lived in New York and died there in 2006.
x-works-progress-administration-poster-art
This poster was made by an artist working for the Works Progress Administration, a New Deal program that hired thousands of artists in the 1930s to make posters, murals and prints for the public.

Alex Colville was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1920. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II, painting the Netherlands and the liberation of Bergen-Belsen, and later became famous for calm, mysterious pictures. He lived in Nova Scotia and died in Wolfville in 2013.

Charles Comfort was a Canadian painter born in Edinburgh, Scotland, in 1900. He grew up in Winnipeg, served as an official war artist in World War II and later became the director of the National Gallery of Canada. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Lawren P. Harris was a Canadian painter born in Toronto in 1910, the son of the Group of Seven painter Lawren Harris. He was an official Canadian war artist in World War II and later a teacher and painter. He died in Ottawa in 1994.

Bruno Bobak was a Canadian painter born in Poland in 1923. He grew up in Canada and served as an official Canadian war artist in World War II, then taught art in Fredericton, New Brunswick, where he lived until his death in 2012.

Molly Bobak was a Canadian painter born in Vancouver in 1920. She was the first woman official war artist in the Canadian army in World War II, married the artist Bruno Bobak, and lived in Fredericton, New Brunswick, until she died in 2014.

William Franklin Draper was an American painter born in Hopedale, Massachusetts, in 1912. He was a combat artist for the US Navy in World War II and later a portrait painter in California. He died in 2003.
x-joseph-gary-sheahan
Joseph Gary Sheahan was an American combat artist who painted watercolors of the US Army during World War II, including a view of Utah Beach in Normandy in 1944.
Sidney Simon was an American painter and sculptor born in Pittsburgh in 1917. He was a combat artist for the US Army in World War II and painted the Japanese surrender in Tokyo Bay. He died in 1997.

Julien Binford was an American painter born in Powhatan County, Virginia, in 1908. He painted for the US Army Air Forces in World War II and later taught art at Mary Washington College in Fredericksburg, Virginia. He died in 1997.

Aaron Bohrod was an American painter born in Chicago in 1907. He served as an official US Army war artist in World War II in the Pacific and Europe and later became the University of Wisconsin's first artist in residence. He died in Madison in 1992.

McClelland Barclay was an American illustrator born in St. Louis in 1891. He became famous for his magazine and poster art, then joined the US Navy as an artist in World War II. He disappeared at sea in 1943 when his ship was sunk.
x-nasa-photograph-by-neil-armstrong

Neil Armstrong, born in 1930 in Ohio, was the commander of Apollo 11 and the first person to walk on the Moon in 1969. Because he carried the camera, most of the famous photographs from the Moon walk show Buzz Aldrin, not him. He died in 2012.
x-nasa-photograph-by-william-anders

William Anders, born in Hong Kong in 1933, was an American astronaut who flew on Apollo 8, the first mission to orbit the Moon, in December 1968. His photograph Earthrise, taken on that flight, became one of the most famous images of the 1900s. He died in 2024.
x-nasa-apollo-17-crew
The Blue Marble was taken by the crew of Apollo 17, Eugene Cernan, Ronald Evans and Harrison Schmitt, on their way to the Moon in December 1972. It was the last Apollo flight to the Moon.
x-nasa

NASA, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration, was created in 1958 and organized the American space program, including the Mercury, Gemini and Apollo missions. Its photographs, made by employees of the US government, belong to the public.
x-nasa-photograph-by-david-scott

David Scott, born in 1932 in Texas, was an American astronaut who flew to the Moon as commander of Apollo 15 in 1971. He took photographs of his crewmate James Irwin on the surface and the lunar rover.

David Fairrington was an American artist born in 1940 who served as a member of the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His paintings of soldiers, helicopters and Vietnamese people are in the US Army art collection.
x-stephen-h-randall

Stephen H. Randall was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army's Vietnam combat art team in 1968. His watercolors of helicopters, soldiers and daily life are in the US Army art collection.
x-ronald-a-wilson

Ronald A. Wilson was an American artist who served as a combat artist with the US Army in Vietnam in 1967. His moody, colorful paintings of night operations and helicopters are in the US Army art collection.
James Pollock was an American artist who served in the US Army's combat art program in Vietnam in 1967. His paintings of the war and the jungle are part of the Army's art collection.
x-unknown-photographer
The photographer who made this picture is not known. Press photographers and news agencies of the early 1900s often did not record the names of the people who took their photographs.

Master Theodoric was a Bohemian painter active in Prague between about 1348 and 1381. He was the court painter of Emperor Charles IV and painted the holy figures for the walls of Karlštejn Castle, which are among the best-known paintings of medieval central Europe.
x-anonymous-illuminator-st-albans-chronicl

This picture of the Battle of Agincourt comes from the St Albans Chronicle, an English history written by the monk Thomas Walsingham. The illustrator is not known, but the manuscript was made soon after the events it shows, in the early 1420s.

Victor Honoré Janssens was a Flemish painter born in Brussels in 1658. He painted historical, mythological and religious pictures for churches and nobles in Brussels, where he lived and worked until he died in 1736.
x-anonymous-illuminator-french-chronicle

This picture comes from a medieval French royal chronicle, painted by an illuminator whose name was not recorded. Manuscripts like this were made by workshops of artists in the 1300s and 1400s for kings and nobles.

Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter, born in the town of 's-Hertogenbosch around 1450. He lived there all his life and painted strange, crowded visions of heaven, hell and human foolishness filled with monsters and tiny details. He died in 's-Hertogenbosch in 1516.
